meaning:
παρά-πτωρμα, -τος, τό
(παραπίπτω), [in LXX for מַעַל, פֶּשַׁע, etc. ;]
1. a false step, a blunder (Polyb.).
2. Ethically, a misdeed, trespass (LXX): Mat.6:14-15, Mrk.11:25-26, Rom.4:25 5:15 ff Rom.11:11-12, 2Co.5:19, Gal.6:1, Eph.1:7 2:1, 5, Col.2:13.†
SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία (AS)

elsewhere.note: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.
who was delivered up for our trespasses, and was raised for our justification.
namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness; looking to yourself so that you also…
in whom we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
You were dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh. He made you alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses,
